summary: A small, mostly behavioral core. Video is a scan-time, per-pixel pipeline driven by Galaxian-style loaded H/V counters, and collision is detected per pixel from the raster counter bits, not in a batch sprite pass like MAME's. The music and laugh audio is built as counter chains and 555 timers named after board locations. Against that, the PC3092/PC3259 custom chips are not modelled as units; their register behaviour (collision +1 offset, 0x07/0x08 status codes, coin/start gating on port 0x08 bit 1) matches MAME's own guesses, so the I/O side reads as copied from MAME.

findings.note: hcnt reloads to 0x0C0 at 0x1FF and vcnt to 0x0F8, like a preset counter chain whose carry drives the load. Blanking and sync are decoded from those counter values (lines 176-208), where MAME only gives raw screen totals.

findings.signal: scan-time tile fetch phased on H counter bits
findings.note: VRAM/colour RAM address, char ROM address and pixel latch are set on successive HCNT(2:0) phases (101/110/111), and pixels are shifted out per pixel clock. This is a board-style fetch pipeline, not MAME's tilemap callback.

findings.signal: per-pixel collision from raster counter bits
findings.note: Collision is latched while scanning, when a background pixel and a sprite pixel coincide, and the address is built from I_VCNT(7:3)&I_HCNT(7:3) (the 128V..8V/128H..8H inputs of PC3259). MAME instead loops over the sprite after drawing the tilemap and reads the bitmap back.

The sprite is drawn by subtracting the sprite position from the live H/V counters and fetching a ROM byte every 8 pixels. It does not use MAME's nested for-y/for-x loop or its flip adjustments (sy+=1, sx+1); registers are stored inverted (not cpu_data_out), unlike MAME's spriteram.

findings.signal: music as counter chain with board-location names
findings.note: W_2CD_Q is an 8-bit counter clocked by an H counter bit that reloads I_TONE on overflow (W_2CD_LDn), feeding a divider W_4E_Q whose bits drive fixed DAC levels. This is a gate-level counter-chain model, where MAME uses the abstract DISCRETE_NOTE node.

The laugh is a left 555 (W_4J_L_OUT) that sweeps a count controlling the period of a right 555 (W_4J_R_OUT), with reset tied to the enable. The structure is the board's oscillator pair, not MAME's discrete netlist nodes.

findings.signal: collision register constants match MAME guesses
findings.note: Register 3 returns x7 for no collision and x8 for a hit, and the collision address is (V/8*32 + H/8) + 1. Both are exactly MAME's values, and MAME's +1 is an empirical fudge, not a modelled chip function.

findings.signal: coin/start gating copied from MAME's guess
findings.note: Port 0x08 bit 0 drives flip and bit 1 (IO_8) gates the upper nibble of IN1. This mirrors MAME's pc3092_data[1]&0x02 test, which MAME itself treats as speculative, rather than modelling the PC3092 chip.

findings.signal: custom chips flattened into port handlers
findings.note: PC3092 and PC3259 have no entities or pin-level ports. Their behaviour sits in an IO_Write/IO_Read case on address, which tracks MAME's address-map handlers and the bit assignments of port_sound_w (including clearing collision on D0).
The address ranges, I/O nibble decode and the inverted colour with an intensity bit are what any correct core must share with MAME.
Explosion/breath/appear are played back from a ROM of samples with a priority scheme. This models neither the SN76477 circuit nor MAME's device parameters.
